summary: A sharp BofA warning comparing AI stocks to the 1990s fiber optic bubble triggered a broad Tech/AI selloff, sending QQQ down ~2.5% and crushing high-beta names like MARA (-9.6%), MSTR (-9.6%), PLTR (-7.2%), and SNOW (-8.4%) as VIX spiked above 22. Capital rotated aggressively into Defense (RTX +3.7%, LMT +3.6%) and Energy (CVX +2.6%) on geopolitical risk from Yemen/Middle East missile strikes and Saudi coalition intercepts. CoreWeave credit stress added contagion fears across AI/cloud names, while AAPL showed rare relative strength on iPhone Duo demand and China's $37B consumer subsidy program.

Capital fled into Defense (RTX +3.7%, LMT +3.6%) and Energy (CVX +2.6%) as Yemen missile strikes and Saudi coalition intercepts provided a textbook geopolitical catalyst. AAPL stood out as the sole resilient core-tech name (+0.43%), supported by strong iPhone demand, China subsidies, and Berkshire activity, while open SELL signals on PLTR and MSTR and BUY signals on RTX, LMT, and AAPL all held at entry.

A deep risk-off rotation is now in its fourth consecutive session, with a $260B+ AI/software unwind (led by PLTR, SNOW, MSTR, MARA) driven by BofA's AI bubble warning, CoreWeave credit contagion, and VIX spiking above 22. Capital is decisively fleeing into Defense (RTX +3.73%, LMT +3.65%) and Energy (CVX +2.59%) on live Middle East escalation via Yemen missile strikes and a US SPR solicitation. MSTR faces added structural headwind from confirmed MSCI index removal forcing passive fund outflows, while AAPL stands as the lone resilient core-tech name amid the broader selloff.

Tech staged a broad oversold bounce led by AI/cloud names — DDOG (+5.4%) and AMZN (+4.98%) surged on high-conviction analyst upgrades (Bernstein and Morgan Stanley respectively), while semis and cloud broadly recovered as the BofA AI bubble panic faded. Defense (RTX, LMT) and financials (JPM) lagged as geopolitical risk premiums eased on Putin-Trump-Xi diplomatic signals and rate expectations shifted. Open signals show DDOG and AMZN as high-confidence BUYs, MSTR SELL holding with crypto-adjacent names still lagging, and PLTR SELL under painful pressure (-4.4%) as Knox Federal deal and AI rebound momentum clash with extreme valuation thesis.

A mixed session saw the Dow rally ~500 points on US-Iran diplomacy hopes while the Nasdaq slipped, with defense (NOC +4.6% on record $110B backlog) and healthcare leading and Big Tech (META, GOOGL, AAPL) dragging as the rally broadened to small caps. NOC's blowout Q3 earnings provide strong fundamental read-across for open RTX and LMT BUY positions, while the MSTR SELL faces mounting pressure as Bitcoin sentiment (Saylor's six-figure BTC call) extends the rally despite intact MSCI outflow headwinds. AAPL's foldable iPhone launch failed to lift shares (-1% on a green Dow day), prompting a downgrade of the open BUY to WATCH pending post-launch demand confirmation or a hold of $335 support.

A broad risk-on reversal drove the Nasdaq +1%, led by AI/cloud and crypto-adjacent names surging on two key catalysts: SpaceX confirming no slowdown in AI compute demand and the OCC finalizing GENIUS Act stablecoin rules. Cybersecurity names DDOG (+6.5%) and NET (+5.3%) also spiked on a critical PHP flaw affecting ~70% of websites, while defense (RTX) and healthcare (JNJ) rotated out as geopolitical risk premiums faded on Ukraine peace talk resumption. Open SELL signals on MSTR and PLTR turned deeply painful at -12.2% and -8.4% respectively, with confidence downgraded to LOW as the structural bull catalysts overwhelmed the original theses.

Nasdaq suffered its worst session since June as a chipmaking equipment supply warning crushed semis (AMD -8.1%, INTC -8.0%) and META's AI spending concerns from earnings dragged the broader growth/AI complex below the 50-day moving average. Capital rotated hard into defense and defensives, with LMT surging nearly 7% on a Q3 earnings blowout and an 850-jet F-35 Pentagon deal, while JNJ caught a safe-haven bid as healthcare outperformed. Active signals favor selling AMD and META on multi-source fundamental headwinds, while reaffirming LMT and JNJ buys; AMZN BUY from Tuesday is -4.6% but held as no stock-specific catalyst has emerged.

A sharply bifurcated session saw Energy and Cybersecurity surge — NET +7.29%, SLB +7.08% — driven by Trump's Iran military threat, Gulf undersea cable sabotage risk, and a PHP vulnerability bid, while Big Tech, Financials, and Healthcare sold off on AI spending anxiety and a Dow -650pt macro risk-off move. Open BUY signals on NET (+6.0%), DDOG (+3.6%), and LMT (+2.4%) are all working, but AMZN BUY was closed at -5.5% and flipped to SELL ahead of earnings with Nasdaq below its 50-day. Capital is rotating defensively into infrastructure security and defense as geopolitical escalation enters day 2 and Big Tech earnings risk mounts.
